findings: The original E3 V1 preregistration no longer has a causally valid Arm A because WP509 generation 2 was accepted after the E2 mapping and materially strengthened the current baseline.

Current WP509 G2 already provides deterministic bounded iteration exit, work-budget exit, unchanged-state OBSERVE, UNKNOWN/CONFLICT preservation through ASK at the iteration limit, explicit HOLD handling, typed exits, COMPLETE-unreachable semantics, and evaluator-origin lineage sealing.
Running the old A/B now would confound candidate benefit with architecture drift and could manufacture an apparent gain against an obsolete baseline.

A narrower residual hypothesis remains plausible: explicit typed evidence-delta semantics POSITIVE|NEGATIVE|NONE|UNKNOWN plus progress_delta may distinguish fresh negative evidence and semantic progress from mere unchanged-state/iteration counters.
Any surviving mechanism must be distilled through the existing WP509 evaluator/control path; a second exit-control authority is not justified.
counterhypothesis: Current WP509 G2 exit semantics already capture nearly all useful stopping benefit; adding explicit progress/evidence-delta logic would add state, thresholds and causal complexity without meaningful incremental reduction in redundant continuation.

must_pin: held-out fixture corpus and deterministic seed before execution
must_cover: unchanged plateau that already triggers G2 OBSERVE
required_next_preregistration.primary_measurement: incremental redundant-transition reduction beyond WP509 G2, not benefit relative to the obsolete pre-G2 baseline
